native_explainer.title: 汉语怎样表达英语 “for” 的不同关系
native_explainer.body: 英语的 for 把目的、受益者、接受者、目的地、原因、时长、交换和期限等不同关系压在一个词里，汉语通常分开表达。表示目的常用“为了/为”，表示受益者可用“为”，口语中给某人东西或替某人做事常用“给”。原因通常用“因为/由于”，目的地常用“到/去”等结构。持续时间往往直接用时间数量短语，如“两个小时”，不需要一个对应 for 的介词；截止时间可用“到……为止/最晚……”。交换常用“用……换……”或“以……换……”。所以不要给 for 找一个固定汉语词，而要先判断它在句子里的关系。

rules.summary_en: 为/为了 commonly marks purpose or the person/cause for whose benefit or sake an action is performed.
tips_en: Ask whether the phrase means for the purpose/sake/benefit of something.
Mandarin 为 can also participate in causal readings, so use the complete construction and context.

rules.summary_en: 给 commonly marks a recipient or person toward whom a transfer/action is directed in many colloquial and standard constructions.
tips_en: If English for identifies who receives something, check a 给 construction.
Recipient marking depends on the verb and word order; do not treat 给 as a universal for-equivalent.

rules.summary_en: 因为/由于 explicitly mark cause or reason.
tips_en: If English for means because of, use a cause construction rather than 为了.
Keep purpose and cause separate even though 为 can occur in both semantic neighborhoods.

forms.display: 到 / 去 / 向 + 目标

rules.summary_en: Destination/goal is expressed by motion and directional constructions such as 到, 去, or 向 rather than by one generic equivalent of for.
tips_en: Choose the construction based on the motion verb and whether the endpoint, direction, or departure is being profiled.
Do not insert 为 merely because English says leave for Shanghai.

forms.display: 时间数量短语（如“两小时”）

rules.summary_en: Duration is often expressed directly with a time-quantity phrase, without a dedicated preposition corresponding to English for.
tips_en: When for answers how long, Mandarin may use a bare duration phrase.
This is a useful reminder that absence of a preposition is itself a real grammatical strategy.

rules.summary_en: Deadline/endpoint meanings use constructions such as 到……为止 or 最晚…… rather than a generic for-equivalent.
tips_en: Distinguish a deadline from a duration.
Use an endpoint construction when the time is the latest target rather than the span of an event.

rules.summary_en: Exchange/substitution is commonly expressed with constructions such as 用…换… or 以…换….
tips_en: If for means in exchange for, look for an exchange verb/construction.
The two things being exchanged occupy construction-specific positions; there is no single free-standing for word.

languages.notes: Mandarin candidate uses Simplified Chinese learner copy while citing Taiwan MOE dictionary evidence that 為 wèi can mark cause, service target/beneficiary, and purpose. Regional lexical preferences require native review.

native_explainer.title: 日本語では英語の「for」をどう表すか
native_explainer.body: 英語の for は、目的・受益者・受け手・行き先・期間・理由・交換・期限などを一語で表すことがありますが、日本語では関係ごとに形が変わります。意図的な目的は「Vために」、人や物のためなら「Nのために」が基本です。受け手や到着点には「に」、期限には「までに」、継続の終点には「まで」を使います。期間は「2時間」のように助詞なしで置けることも多く、理由の「ため（に）」は目的の「ために」と文脈で区別します。交換や代替は「～と引き換えに／～の代わりに」など別の構文になります。for を一語で訳すのではなく、まず意味関係を見ます。

rules.summary_en: ために expresses intentional purpose with a verb and purpose/benefit/sake relationships with a noun phrase.
tips_en: With an intentional action goal, Vために is a core purpose pattern.
Nのために can mean for the sake/benefit of N, so identify whether the noun is a beneficiary or a purpose domain.

rules.summary_en: に marks recipients with transfer verbs and destinations/arrival goals with many motion verbs.
tips_en: The same particle participates in multiple case roles, so use the verb frame to identify recipient versus destination.
Do not translate English for first; identify the Japanese case role required by the verb.

rules.summary_en: ため/ために can mark cause or reason in causal constructions, distinct from intentional-purpose ために.
tips_en: Context and the form before ため distinguish reason from an intentional goal.
If the sentence describes what caused a result, read ため causally rather than as in order to.

forms.display: 時間数量句（「2時間」など） / ～の間

rules.summary_en: Japanese often expresses duration with a bare time-quantity phrase; ～の間 can explicitly profile the interval during which something holds.
tips_en: A bare duration phrase can be grammatical without a particle corresponding to English for.
Use 間 when the interval itself is being framed as during that period.

rules.summary_en: までに marks a deadline by which an event must occur; まで marks an endpoint up to which a state/action continues.
tips_en: までに is a completion deadline, while まで is an endpoint of continuation.
This distinction is exactly why English for/by/until should not be collapsed into one Japanese form.

rules.summary_en: Exchange and substitution use constructions such as ～と引き換えに and ～の代わりに.
tips_en: Choose 引き換え for an exchange/countervalue and 代わり for replacement/substitution.
Do not try to reuse ために for exchange meanings.

rules.summary_en: Support/favor is typically expressed lexically with constructions built around 賛成する or 支持する rather than a preposition equivalent to for.
tips_en: When English for means in favor of, switch to a support verb/construction.
Japanese often lexicalizes this relation instead of marking it with a single particle.

languages.notes: Japan Foundation learning materials support the purpose/reason and まで/までに distinctions used here; full candidate still requires Japanese-native review.

native_explainer.title: 한국어에서는 영어 ‘for’를 어떻게 표현할까
native_explainer.body: 영어의 for는 목적, 수혜자, 받는 이, 목적지, 기간, 이유, 교환, 마감 시점 등을 한 단어로 나타낼 수 있지만 한국어에서는 관계에 따라 표현이 달라집니다. 목적이나 ‘누구를 위해’의 뜻은 보통 ‘-기 위해(서)’ 또는 ‘N을/를 위해(서)’로 나타냅니다. 사람에게 가는 물건이나 행동의 받는 이는 ‘에게/한테/께’, 목적지는 흔히 ‘에’를 씁니다. 이유는 ‘때문에’, 기간은 ‘동안’, 마감·끝점은 ‘까지’가 대표적입니다. 교환·대가는 ‘대가로’, 대체는 ‘대신(에)’처럼 따로 표현합니다. for 자체를 번역하지 말고 문장에서 어떤 관계인지 먼저 판단해야 합니다.

rules.summary_en: 위해(서) constructions mark an intended purpose or acting for the benefit/sake of a person or thing.
tips_en: Use -기 위해(서) when the goal is an action.
With a noun, N을/를 위해(서) highlights whose sake or benefit motivates the action.

rules.summary_en: 에게/한테/께 mark an animate recipient or target in common transfer/communication constructions, with 께 honorific.
tips_en: If English for means the person receiving something, use the Korean recipient particle selected by register.
Do not replace recipient marking with 위해 just because English uses for.

rules.summary_en: 에 marks a destination or endpoint with many motion verbs.
tips_en: With motion, ask where the movement ends.
The verb and case particle determine the Korean construction, not the English preposition.

rules.summary_en: 때문에 marks cause or reason.
tips_en: If English for means because of, a 때문에 construction is a core option.
Keep cause separate from intentional purpose expressed with 위해(서).

rules.summary_en: 동안 marks the time span during which something continues or occurs.
tips_en: Use 동안 when for answers how long/during what period.
Do not confuse duration with the endpoint marked by 까지.

rules.summary_en: 까지 marks an endpoint or limit and is used in deadline expressions depending on the predicate/context.
tips_en: Think up to/as far as an endpoint.
For an explicit by-deadline, combine the endpoint expression with the verb/aspect that requires completion.

rules.summary_en: 대가로 expresses countervalue/payment; 대신(에) expresses replacement or doing something in another's place.
tips_en: Separate countervalue from substitution even though English can use for in both.
Use 대가로 for what is received as a price/countervalue and 대신 for replacement.

rules.summary_en: Support/favor is usually expressed with support verbs such as 찬성하다 or 지지하다 rather than a dedicated for-like particle.
tips_en: When English for means in favor of, switch to a lexical support construction.
The case marking around the supported proposal/person follows the selected verb.

languages.notes: Korean learner-dictionary evidence plus construction-level synthesis. Register and particle selection require Korean-native review before stronger trust promotion.
